morning-rules.body: Early outdoor light within 30 minutes of waking helps anchor your circadian rhythm — many explorers report fewer afternoon crashes when they pair sunlight with a short morning stretch.
Delay your first caffeine by about 90 minutes after waking so natural cortisol can peak; this often softens the mid-afternoon rebound crash.
Five minutes of morning movement — even light stretching — increases blood flow and tends to sustain focus through the post-lunch dip.
A brief meditation before email can lower perceived afternoon fatigue; explorers who log it consistently see steadier energy scores by week 3.
Add rules one at a time: master sunlight plus stretching for a week before introducing caffeine offset or meditation.

eating.body: Log your natural eating window for two full weeks before narrowing — baseline timing makes your personalised trial report much clearer.
Keep water and black tea or coffee outside the window if it helps hunger; consistency matters more than perfection on day one.
A stable first meal time anchors circadian metabolism — explorers with fixed breakfast see smoother afternoon energy curves.
Rate afternoon energy at the same clock time each day so week-to-week comparisons in your trial report stay reliable.
When moving to an 8-hour window, aim to finish your last meal at least three hours before bed for better sleep and next-day energy.

screen-sleep.body: Switch phones to a warm night shift after sunset even before your screen-free window — it reduces melatonin suppression in the last hour awake.
Replace in-bed scrolling with a paper book or calm audio; explorers cut sleep-onset time most when screens leave the bedroom entirely.
Build your wind-down in stages: 30 minutes screen-free in weeks 3–4, then extend to 60 minutes — sudden jumps are harder to sustain.
Charge devices outside the bedroom so late-night checks are less tempting and sleep quality scores improve faster.
Morning outdoor light the day after a screen-light evening helps pull your clock earlier and reinforces earlier melatonin onset.

relaxation.body: Vagal breathing (roughly 4 seconds in, 6 out) for two minutes can lower same-day stress scores — useful before meetings or school runs.
Progressive muscle relaxation works best at a fixed daily time; explorers who pair it with bedtime see the largest anxiety drop by week 4.
Even a 10-minute nature walk counts — green exposure plus light movement reduces rumination in a single session for many people.
Log which practice you used each day so your week-6 personalised trial report can show what worked best for you.
Stack one practice onto an existing habit (e.g. breathing after lunch) to raise adherence without adding a new time block.

upf-mood.body: Swap one UPF-heavy snack per week rather than overhauling every meal — gradual change sticks and mood logs stay interpretable.
Watch for emulsifiers and maltodextrin on labels as quick UPF markers when you are estimating daily UPF percentage.
Batch-cook one unprocessed lunch for weekdays — explorers cut lunch UPF fastest without changing breakfast or dinner at first.
Note mood before and after meals occasionally to spot which swaps correlate with calmer afternoons.
Add beans, oats, or leafy greens once a day — fibre supports gut–brain signalling linked to steadier baseline mood.

morning-rules.body: Across 78 active participants, afternoon energy improves most when explorers log 3+ morning rules before noon. Your data is contributing to this finding.
morning-rules.highlight: Open-access cohort study in preparation · Data collection until May 2026

morning-rules.body: Explorers who log sunlight alone on 5+ days per week average 0.8 points higher afternoon energy than low-sunlight weeks.
Early analysis suggests caffeine offset adopters report fewer “severe” afternoon crashes, especially when combined with morning movement.
Morning meditation shows the strongest link to lower afternoon fatigue when paired with sunlight — not necessarily when done alone.
Your anonymised logs feed the morning rules personalised trial cohort — publication will acknowledge citizen science contributors.

eating.body: Among 64 explorers, a consistent 10-hour eating window is associated with steadier afternoon glucose and fewer energy dips vs baseline weeks.
eating.highlight: Citizen science dataset · metabolic timing arm

eating.body: By week 4, most participants who maintain their window report higher mean afternoon energy than baseline (+1.1 points average).
Earlier first meal times (before 9am) correlate with better sleep quality scores in explorers also tracking rest — a possible crossover effect.
Combined time-restricted eating data will support an open-access pre-print on circadian meal timing and daily energy.
Hunger comfort ratings typically normalise by day 10–14 once the window stabilises — useful context for your trial report.

screen-sleep.body: 51 explorers tracking evening screens: a 30-minute screen-free window before bed links to faster sleep onset in week 3–4 logs.
Moving to 60 minutes screen-free plus no in-bed use is associated with +1.4 points mean sleep quality vs baseline.
Evening blue-light exposure remains the strongest predictor of later sleep midpoint in this cohort.
Explorers who add morning outdoor light see larger sleep gains from the same evening screen changes.
Your logs support an upcoming open publication on screen habits and restorative sleep architecture.

relaxation.body: 58 participants: days with 2+ relaxation practices show lower mean stress and anxiety than baseline weeks.
Vagal breathing has the fastest same-week stress reduction; PMR shows the largest trait change by weeks 4–6.
Short nature walks reduce same-day rumination scores even when stress was high that morning.
Meditation plus PMR on the same day is linked to the highest composure scores in the cohort so far.
Aggregated relaxation data will feed a citizen science paper on low-cost stress interventions in daily life.

upf-mood.body: In the UPF reduction cohort (n=22), explorers cutting UPF by 15+ percentage points report higher mean mood by week 5.
Swaps at breakfast show the strongest short-term mood lift — possibly via steadier morning glucose.
Lower UPF weeks correlate with less mood volatility (smaller day-to-day swings) for active loggers.
Gut–brain mechanisms are being summarised for a plain-language science brief linked to this exploration.
upf-mood.highlight: Evidence review · Dr Priya Nair team

upf-mood.body: Your UPF and mood logs contribute to an open dataset on ultra-processed food and daily wellbeing.
